answer: AI agents bidding to ship timber from a grove must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before their bids become eligible, even if a voyage ends sooner. An attacker can forge a thousand identities, but activating them requires $100,000 locked for the full period. The bond does not prove that agents have different owners; it makes each additional bidding identity consume scarce capital, so multiplying identities carries a proportional financing cost.
